bullets.title: ACN +5% premarket: Investor Day 3-year guide beats Street on growth & margins
bullets.body: Accenture introduced FY27-29 guidance at its first Analyst Day since 2022: mid-single-digit revenue growth in FY27-28, mid-to-high single-digit in FY29 (UBS models +6% vs +4.8% Street), with 10-30bps annual operating margin expansion and FCF/NI ≥1.1x. FY27 cash return of at least $9.5B including $5.5B buybacks; stock up ~4-5% premarket. UBS maintains Buy, calling guidance a de-risking of prior AI-related investor concerns.

bullets.title: Barclays triple-downgrade: DELL/HPE/NTAP cut to Equal Weight on enterprise IT spending concerns
bullets.body: Barclays analyst Tim Long downgraded all three to Equal Weight from Overweight: DELL PT cut to $574 from $603 (-2.7% pre-mkt), HPE PT cut to $77 from $83 (-4.0% pre-mkt), NTAP PT held at $219 (-3.6% pre-mkt). Cited weak enterprise IT spending environment.

bullets.title: META: multiple PT raises to $860-$895 on AI ad monetization; consensus very bullish
bullets.body: Goldman raises META to Buy with $860 PT (from $725) on AI-driven creative/targeting/measurement improvements; UBS raises PT to $884 from $715 citing Advantage+, Reels, Business Agents; Citi raises to $895 on clearer superintelligence product roadmap and updated 2027 expense projections. 3Q revenue projected +25% Y/Y ex-FX. META reports Wed Oct 21 after close; consensus EPS $6.76, revenue $63.3B.

bullets.title: GOOGL +1.3% premarket on Gemini 4 Argon launch; digital ad checks positive
bullets.body: Google launched Gemini 4 Argon globally at $2/M input and $10/M output tokens, ranking #1 on Vals Index across finance, coding, legal, and tax. UBS ad checks show better-than-expected 3Q digital ad environment with YouTube a standout; UBS keeps GOOGL Neutral on rising AI capex and GenAI search competition. Citi raises 2027E GCP revenue +7% to $219B on TPU ramp (~$97B TPU-related GCP revenue 2026E-27E) while maintaining $447 PT.

bullets.title: MSFT: Citi raises PT to $636; Azure to accelerate 46-47% YoY in FQ1 as Copilot adoption surges
bullets.body: Citi raises MSFT PT to $636 (Buy), expecting ~2pt Azure beat in FQ1 to 46-47% YoY cc growth with Azure AI contributing ~25pts. Reseller survey shows NTM growth expectations at 16%, up 5pts q/q. FY27 capex seen at $237B (+63% YoY). Separately, Azure division head is asking leaders to develop plans for 20% cost cuts across ~11,500-person division, flagging spend discipline amid AI investment pressure.

bullets.title: AMZN: Citi projects AWS +40% YoY in 3Q with continued margin expansion
bullets.body: Citi projects AWS revenue growth of +40% Y/Y in 3Q led by AI demand with continued North America retail margin expansion. Focus for upcoming earnings: AI product adoption, compute capacity insights, and 2027 CapEx/expense guidance. Risks include Middle East conflict and EU regulatory pressures limiting 4Q guidance.

bullets.title: NOW: Citi raises PT to $170; partner checks show improving AI SKU adoption and federal demand
bullets.body: Citi raises NOW PT to $170 from $154 (21x FY28 EV/FCF), lifting FY27-28 revenue estimates and subscription growth to ~20%. Partner checks show improving sentiment on new AI SKUs; federal partner reported strong 20% Y/Y growth with urgency ahead of elections. Management tone on Decagon: ServiceNow COO explicitly denied strategic interest in acquisition; investors relieved given recent $11B+ M&A. Jefferies also views NOW-Decagon deal debate as manageable.

bullets.title: NVDA/AMD: Semis on 5-7 day losing streak; custom silicon risk from hyperscalers rising
bullets.body: SOX down 5-7 consecutive sessions (longest since May 2025) as sentiment deteriorates on power scarcity, frontier lab funding viability, and custom chip competition. GS spec sales desk notes Meta, Google, and Microsoft Maia 300 raising risk of value shift away from Nvidia/AMD. MU and SNDK each down ~7% over the streak; SK Hynix delays HBM4 back-end equipment orders to 2027, a negative read for the memory supply chain.

bullets.title: ORCL: Project Jupiter on schedule; pipeline reroute may avoid BLM delay; no FY27 impact
bullets.body: Mizuho maintains Outperform on ORCL: Project Jupiter has 4,300+ workers deployed, $13B projected economic impact, and 850MW delivered in FQ1 with ~1.2GW expected in FY26. Former BLM director indicates proposed pipeline reroute could avoid restarting environmental review. Management reaffirmed no impact on FY27 revenue/earnings guidance. Further updates expected at Oct 28 Investor Day.

bullets.title: T: Selling AT&T Mexico to Televisa/Fintech for $2B at a surprisingly low 2.3x EV/EBITDA
bullets.body: AT&T agreed to divest AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings for $2.0B cash, closing Q1 2027 subject to Mexican regulatory approvals. Implied valuation of 2.3x EV/EBITDA (based on ~$875M 2026 EBITDA estimate) characterized as surprisingly low. T earnings call scheduled Oct 21 at 8:30am ET; consensus Q3 EPS $0.60, revenue $31.69B.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM raises estimates, reiterates OW at $200; 3Q revenue +33% projected
bullets.body: JPM raised SHOP estimates ~1-3% on strong execution; projects 3Q revenue growth +33% and 4Q +34%, with gross profit dollar growth +29-30%. Reiterated Overweight with $200 PT citing agentic commerce bull case and ~30% 2027E revenue growth path. SHOP is JPM's top pick alongside TTWO.

bullets.title: RBLX: Multiple PT raises on stronger engagement/monetization; DA Davidson stays Neutral
bullets.body: UBS raises RBLX PT to $53 on stronger engagement and monetization driven by 'Steal an Egg'; JPM raises estimates 3-7% reflecting algo changes, solid CCU data, and improved monetization (projects 3Q bookings -10% vs -14% to -18% guide). D.A. Davidson rates Neutral while modeling 2027 DAU scenarios.

bullets.title: TTWO: Multiple desks bullish into GTA VI; stock down 17% vs +18% Red Dead 2 cycle at same stage
bullets.body: Jefferies reiterates Buy at $200 PT, modeling $12 EPS FY28; notes stock at 20x P/E near YTD lows. JPM says PC version launching Q1'27 (only months after console) is better-than-feared. UBS calls TTWO most constructive pick on rising GTA VI demand indicators with FY27 estimates raised. Stock fell 4% on GTA VI hack/leak concerns but multiple desks see current weakness as entry point.

bullets.title: NFLX: Citi recommends calls into earnings; consensus EPS $0.82, revenue $12.87B (reports Oct 20)
bullets.body: Citi's derivatives desk recommends NFLX calls, arguing engagement concerns are overblown and gaming downloads improved from #25 in June to #5 in July. UBS 3Q earnings brief notes NFLX among 40 companies reporting in the next 5 trading days. Separately, JPM flags US churn rising in Q3 as a cautious data point.

bullets.title: MSFT/AMZN dominate Citi CIO survey as top AI wallet-share gainers; IT budgets accelerate to +3.4%
bullets.body: Citi global CIO survey shows NTM IT budget growth at +3.4% (US +3.9%), with 41% of CIOs reporting upward revisions vs 28% last quarter. AI now ~7% of enterprise IT budgets with 72% funded from new budgets. Microsoft cited most frequently as vendor expected to gain AI spending share, followed by Amazon. 63% of CIOs anticipate AI-related headcount reductions.

bullets.title: GOOGL/BE: AEP investing $4B in 702-MW Bloom Energy fuel cell project under 20-year Google PPA
bullets.body: AEP will invest ~$4B in a 702-MW fuel cell project near Cheyenne, Wyoming using Bloom Energy technology; Google secures power via a 20-year PPA. Construction starts 2026 with full operations by end of 2028. This follows a similar Google agreement with Black Hills Corp effective Sept 30, 2026.

bullets.title: AMD: Credit support anchor for $6.5B TensorWave data-center lease; Phase 1 delivery H2 2027
bullets.body: Fermi signed a binding 15-year lease with TensorWave for a 222-MW data center in Carson County, Texas with total contracted revenue of ~$6.5B. AMD provides credit support for Phase 1, a key financing milestone. Partnership framework supports expansion to 650 MW across three phases; Phase 1 occupancy targeted for 4Q27.

bullets.title: HUBS: New EMEA pricing model + 7% workforce reduction reaffirm guidance but raise cost-visibility concerns
bullets.body: HubSpot launched new platform-based pricing in EMEA on Oct 1 and announced a ~7% workforce reduction (~660 employees) while reaffirming guidance. Oppenheimer notes the new pricing model simplifies upmarket adoption but raises near-term cost-visibility concerns. HUBS is down in pre-market alongside broader tech weakness.

bullets.title: NFLX/META/TXN/T/OMC earnings calendar: key reports Oct 20-21
bullets.body: Upcoming consensus estimates: NFLX Oct 20 after close (EPS $0.82, rev $12.87B); OMC Oct 20 after close (EPS $2.67, rev $6.21B); T Oct 21 before open (EPS $0.60, rev $31.69B); META Oct 21 after close (EPS $6.76, rev $63.30B); TXN Oct 21 after close (EPS $2.42, rev $5.92B).

bullets.title: Piper app-software survey: MSFT and NOW best net results; security favors TEAM; 90% at/above plan
bullets.body: 90% of app-software channel partners at or above plan in 3Q26 with MSFT and NOW showing best net results. Security software net scores at highest levels since 2021; Piper favors TEAM and VRNS into earnings. 75% of respondents saw extended sales cycles (vs 78% in 2Q); 36% cite AI project prioritization as driver of deal push-outs.
